title: Which Proteins are Synthesised?
page_title: Which Proteins are Synthesised? | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Biology Revision Notes 2021

blocks.name: Control of gene expression: Extended
blocks.definition:
Explain that most body cells in an organism contain the same genes, but many genes in a particular cell are not expressed because the cell only makes the specific proteins it needs
Describe a haploid nucleus as a nucleus containing a single set of chromosomes
Describe a diploid nucleus as a nucleus containing two sets of chromosomes
State that in a diploid cell, there is a pair of each type of chromosome and in a human diploid cell there are pairs

blocks.md:
- **Expression **of a gene means whether that gene is[ transcribed and translated](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/biology/cie/23/revision-notes/17-inheritance/17-1-inheritance-genes-and-cell-division/17-1-4-protein-synthesis/?_ai=internal-linking) in a particular cell or not
- Most genes are not expressed in a particular cell; they are 'switched off'
- Only the genes whose proteins are vital to that cell's function are expressed ('switched on')

blocks.alt: Protein synthesis, IGCSE & GCSE Biology revision notes
blocks.caption: Protein synthesis

blocks.md:
- In this way, DNA **controls cell function** by **controlling the production of proteins**
- The proteins may be **enzymes, antibodies, **or** receptors **for** neurotransmitters**
- Although all body cells in an organism contain the same genes, **many genes in a particular cell are not expressed** because **the cell only makes the specific proteins it needs**

blocks.alt: Diagram of translation showing mRNA codons in a ribosome, tRNA anticodons bringing amino acids, and peptide bonds forming a growing polypeptide chain.
blocks.caption: The triplet code of DNA (carried by mRNA) is read by the ribosome and amino acids are attached together in a specific sequence to form the protein

blocks.md:
- All humans have **23 different chromosomes** in each cell
- Human body cells, not including the gametes (sex cells), contain two copies of each chromosome, leading to a total of **46 chromosomes**
- Nuclei with two sets of chromosomes are known as **diploid nuclei**
- The **gametes** (egg and sperm cells) only have one copy of each chromosome, meaning they have a** total of 23 chromosomes** in each cell
- Nuclei with one set of unpaired chromosomes are known as **haploid nuclei**

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
An easy way to remember the difference between haploid and diploid is to remember:

<u>**Ha**</u>ploid = <u>**Ha**</u>lf the normal number of chromosomes

It’s worth noting that the human diploid chromosome number is 46. In an exam, you may be given information about a different species, with a different number of chromosomes. Make sure you read exam questions carefully.
